from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Section Title and Lecture Lines from Shared State
        title_text = "Prerequisite: The Bernoulli Trial"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Imagine a single event with only two possible outcomes.",
            "We call this simple building block a Bernoulli trial.",
            "Success has probability p, while failure has probability q."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        FROG_COLOR = "#55FF55"
        FLY_COLOR = "#888888"
        SUCCESS_COLOR = "#55FF55"
        FAILURE_COLOR = "#FF5555"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Imagine a single event with only two possible outcomes.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Create Frog (Procedural representation)
        frog_body = Circle(radius=0.35, color=FROG_COLOR, fill_opacity=1)
        frog_eye_l = Dot(radius=0.07, color=BLACK).move_to(frog_body.get_center() + 0.15*UP + 0.12*LEFT)
        frog_eye_r = Dot(radius=0.07, color=BLACK).move_to(frog_body.get_center() + 0.15*UP + 0.12*RIGHT)
        frog = VGroup(frog_body, frog_eye_l, frog_eye_r)
        
        # Create Fly (Procedural representation)
        fly_body = Dot(radius=0.08, color=FLY_COLOR)
        fly_wing_l = Ellipse(width=0.12, height=0.06, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.4).move_to(fly_body.get_center() + 0.08*LEFT + 0.04*UP)
        fly_wing_r = Ellipse(width=0.12, height=0.06, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.4).move_to(fly_body.get_center() + 0.08*RIGHT + 0.04*UP)
        fly = VGroup(fly_body, fly_wing_l, fly_wing_r)

        # Position objects in Col 3 and 5 (leaving Col 2 as a buffer)
        self.place_at_grid(frog, "C3")
        self.place_at_grid(fly, "C5")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(frog, shift=RIGHT), FadeIn(fly, shift=LEFT))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # We call this simple building block a Bernoulli trial.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Label the setup in Row A (Area-Positioning Rule)
        trial_label = Text("Bernoulli Trial", font_size=28, color=BLUE)
        self.place_in_area(trial_label, "A3", "A5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Write(trial_label))
        # Highlight the trial components using Indicate (L004)
        self.play(Indicate(frog, color=YELLOW), Indicate(fly, color=YELLOW))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Success has probability p, while failure has probability q.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Prepare success/failure labels
        success_label = Text("Success", font_size=24, color=SUCCESS_COLOR)
        prob_p = MathTex("p", color=SUCCESS_COLOR)
        failure_label = Text("Failure", font_size=24, color=FAILURE_COLOR)
        prob_q = MathTex("q = 1 - p", color=FAILURE_COLOR)
        
        # Position labels near targets (within 1 grid unit, L003)
        self.place_at_grid(success_label, "B5", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(prob_p, "B4", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(failure_label, "E5", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_in_area(prob_q, "E3", "E4", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        frog_home_pos = frog.get_center().copy()
        
        # Part A: Successful Catch
        self.play(
            frog.animate.move_to(fly.get_center()),
            FadeOut(fly, shift=UP),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.play(
            Write(success_label),
            Write(prob_p)
        )
        self.wait(1.5)
        
        # Reset for Failure Demo
        self.play(
            frog.animate.move_to(frog_home_pos),
            FadeIn(fly),
            success_label.animate.set_fill(opacity=0.3),
            prob_p.animate.set_fill(opacity=0.3),
            run_time=0.8
        )
        
        # Part B: Failure Miss
        # Frog jumps but misses target (moves to D5 instead of C5)
        miss_pos = self.grid["D5"]
        self.play(
            frog.animate.move_to(miss_pos),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.play(
            Write(failure_label),
            Write(prob_q)
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Section Title and Lecture Lines
        title_text = "The B.I.N.S. Criteria"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Binomial distributions must meet four specific criteria, called BINS.",
            "\"B\" stands for Binary: outcomes are either success or failure.",
            "\"I\" means Independent: one trial doesn't affect the next.",
            "\"N\" is for Number: there's a fixed amount of trials.",
            "\"S\" stands for Same: the probability p remains constant."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors
        COLOR_ACRONYM = "#FFFFFF"
        COLOR_CRITERIA = "#AAAAAA"
        COLOR_ROBOT = "#CCCCCC"
        COLOR_SUCCESS = "#55FF55"
        COLOR_HIGHLIGHT = "#FFFF00"
        
        # --- Mobject Creation ---
        # Acronym B-I-N-S
        b_let = Text("B", color=COLOR_ACRONYM)
        i_let = Text("I", color=COLOR_ACRONYM)
        n_let = Text("N", color=COLOR_ACRONYM)
        s_let = Text("S", color=COLOR_ACRONYM)
        
        self.place_at_grid(b_let, "B2", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(i_let, "C2", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(n_let, "D2", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(s_let, "E2", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        bins_vgroup = VGroup(b_let, i_let, n_let, s_let)
        
        # Criteria labels
        binary_label = Text("Binary", color=COLOR_CRITERIA)
        independent_label = Text("Independent", color=COLOR_CRITERIA)
        number_label = Text("Number", color=COLOR_CRITERIA)
        same_label = Text("Same", color=COLOR_CRITERIA)
        
        # Align them to the left of column 3
        labels = [binary_label, independent_label, number_label, same_label]
        row_ids = ["B", "C", "D", "E"]
        for label, row in zip(labels, row_ids):
            self.place_at_grid(label, f"{row}3", scale_factor=0.7)
            label.align_to(self.grid[f"{row}3"], LEFT)
            
        # Robot example (Simple geometric composition)
        robot_body = Rectangle(height=1.0, width=0.7, color=COLOR_ROBOT, fill_opacity=0.6)
        robot_head = Square(side_length=0.35, color=COLOR_ROBOT, fill_opacity=0.6).next_to(robot_body, UP, buff=0.1)
        robot_arm = Line(ORIGIN, RIGHT * 0.4, color=COLOR_ROBOT).next_to(robot_body, RIGHT, buff=0, aligned_edge=UP)
        robot = VGroup(robot_body, robot_head, robot_arm)
        self.place_in_area(robot, "B4", "E5", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        # Ball and Checkmarks
        ball = Circle(radius=0.12, color=ORANGE, fill_opacity=1.0)
        checkmarks = VGroup(*[
            Text("✓", color=COLOR_SUCCESS, font_size=24) for _ in range(5)
        ]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        self.place_at_grid(checkmarks, "F3", scale_factor=0.8) # Row F avoided for labeled objects, but F3 is fine for passive visual feedback

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Binomial distributions must meet four specific criteria, called BINS.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_HIGHLIGHT))
        self.play(Write(bins_vgroup))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "B" stands for Binary: outcomes are either success or failure.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_HIGHLIGHT)
        )
        self.play(
            Indicate(b_let),
            FadeIn(binary_label, shift=RIGHT)
        )
        # Show robot as the Binary example (Success/Miss)
        self.play(FadeIn(robot))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "I" means Independent: one trial doesn't affect the next.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_HIGHLIGHT)
        )
        self.play(
            Indicate(i_let),
            FadeIn(independent_label, shift=RIGHT)
        )
        # Visual hint for independence
        self.play(robot.animate.shift(UP * 0.1), run_time=0.3)
        self.play(robot.animate.shift(DOWN * 0.1), run_time=0.3)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # "N" is for Number: there's a fixed amount of trials.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(COLOR_HIGHLIGHT)
        )
        self.play(
            Indicate(n_let),
            FadeIn(number_label, shift=RIGHT)
        )
        n_label = Text("n = 5", color=WHITE, font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(n_label, "B5", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(n_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # "S" stands for Same: the probability p remains constant.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(COLOR_HIGHLIGHT)
        )
        self.play(
            Indicate(s_let),
            FadeIn(same_label, shift=RIGHT)
        )
        p_label = Text("p = 0.70", color=WHITE, font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(p_label, "C5", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(p_label))
        
        # Action: Shooting 5 times
        ball.move_to(robot_arm.get_end())
        self.play(FadeIn(ball))
        for i in range(5):
            self.play(
                ball.animate.move_to(self.grid["B6"]).set_opacity(0),
                run_time=0.4,
                rate_func=exponential_decay
            )
            self.play(FadeIn(checkmarks[i], scale=1.2), run_time=0.2)
            ball.move_to(robot_arm.get_end()).set_opacity(1)
        
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Retrieve title and lines from storyboard/outline
        title_text = "Visualizing Combinations: The 'How Many Ways' Logic"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Multiple trials create many different paths to the same result.",
            "A tree diagram helps visualize these branching possibilities.",
            "For two shots, there are two ways to hit once.",
            "We use the combination formula to count these unique paths.",
            "This explains why middle outcomes often have higher probabilities."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Colors - using light, distinguishable hex codes
        COLOR_1 = WHITE
        COLOR_2 = "#88FFFF"  # Light Cyan
        COLOR_3 = "#FFFF55"  # Yellow (from storyboard)
        COLOR_4 = "#AAFFAA"  # Light Green
        COLOR_5 = "#FFCC88"  # Light Orange/Gold

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_1)
        root_dot = Dot(color=COLOR_1)
        self.place_at_grid(root_dot, "C2")
        # Label "Start" near root - Using place_at_grid for precise positioning (L003)
        start_label = Text("Start", font_size=20, color=COLOR_1)
        self.place_at_grid(start_label, "C1", scale_factor=0.8) # Left of root in Col 1
        
        self.play(FadeIn(root_dot), Write(start_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_2)
        
        # Branch level 1 (Trial 1)
        s1_node = Dot(color=COLOR_2)
        f1_node = Dot(color=COLOR_2)
        self.place_at_grid(s1_node, "B3")
        self.place_at_grid(f1_node, "D3")
        
        l1_s = Line(root_dot.get_center(), s1_node.get_center(), color=COLOR_2)
        l1_f = Line(root_dot.get_center(), f1_node.get_center(), color=COLOR_2)
        
        # S/F labels on branches - placed within 1 grid unit (L003)
        s1_label = Text("S", font_size=18, color=COLOR_2).next_to(l1_s.get_center(), UP, buff=0.1)
        f1_label = Text("F", font_size=18, color=COLOR_2).next_to(l1_f.get_center(), DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(
            Create(l1_s), Create(l1_f),
            FadeIn(s1_node), FadeIn(f1_node),
            Write(s1_label), Write(f1_label)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_3)
        
        # Branch level 2 (Trial 2)
        nodes_l2 = VGroup(*[Dot(color=COLOR_3) for _ in range(4)])
        positions_l2 = ["B4", "C4", "D4", "E4"]
        for node, pos in zip(nodes_l2, positions_l2):
            self.place_at_grid(node, pos)
            
        l2_lines = VGroup(
            Line(s1_node.get_center(), nodes_l2[0].get_center(), color=COLOR_3), # To SS
            Line(s1_node.get_center(), nodes_l2[1].get_center(), color=COLOR_3), # To SF
            Line(f1_node.get_center(), nodes_l2[2].get_center(), color=COLOR_3), # To FS
            Line(f1_node.get_center(), nodes_l2[3].get_center(), color=COLOR_3)  # To FF
        )
        
        # Final outcome labels - Col 5 is safe from Col 6 clipping (L003)
        outcomes = VGroup(
            Text("SS", font_size=24, color=COLOR_3),
            Text("SF", font_size=24, color=COLOR_3),
            Text("FS", font_size=24, color=COLOR_3),
            Text("FF", font_size=24, color=COLOR_3)
        )
        out_pos = ["B5", "C5", "D5", "E5"]
        for out, pos in zip(outcomes, out_pos):
            self.place_at_grid(out, pos)

        self.play(
            Create(l2_lines),
            FadeIn(nodes_l2),
            Write(outcomes)
        )
        
        # Bracket middle outcomes SF and FS (from storyboard)
        bracket = Brace(VGroup(outcomes[1], outcomes[2]), direction=RIGHT, color=COLOR_3)
        ways_label = Text("2 Ways", font_size=22, color=COLOR_3).next_to(bracket, RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        
        self.play(Create(bracket), Write(ways_label))
        self.play(Indicate(outcomes[1]), Indicate(outcomes[2])) # Using Indicate (L004)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(COLOR_4)
        
        # Combination Formula nCr = 2C1
        formula = MathTex(r"\binom{2}{1} = 2", color=COLOR_4)
        # Positioned in a clear area, avoiding Row F (L003)
        self.place_in_area(formula, "E2", "E4", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color(COLOR_5)
        
        # Highlight paths for exactly 1 success (SF and FS)
        path_sf = VGroup(l1_s, l2_lines[1])
        path_fs = VGroup(l1_f, l2_lines[2])
        
        # Visualizing why middle outcomes have higher probability
        self.play(
            path_sf.animate.set_stroke(color=COLOR_5, width=8),
            path_fs.animate.set_stroke(color=COLOR_5, width=8),
            outcomes[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_5),
            outcomes[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_5),
            ways_label.animate.set_color(COLOR_5)
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from shared state
        title_text = "The Binomial Formula Breakdown"
        lecture_lines = [
            "The formula calculates the probability of exactly k successes.",
            "First, count the number of ways to get k successes.",
            "Next, multiply by the probability of those successes occurring.",
            "Then, multiply by the probability of the remaining failures.",
            "Together, these three parts form the complete binomial equation."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # Define colors from storyboard
        COLOR_WAYS = "#FFA500" # Orange
        COLOR_SUCCESS = "#0000FF" # Blue
        COLOR_FAILURE = "#FF0000" # Red
        COLOR_MAIN = WHITE

        # Create formula with sub-parts for coloring
        # P(X=k) = (n \choose k) p^k q^{n-k}
        # Using a raw string for LaTeX
        formula = MathTex(
            r"P(X=k)",        # 0
            r"=",             # 1
            r"\binom{n}{k}",  # 2
            r"p^k",           # 3
            r"q^{n-k}",       # 4
            color=COLOR_MAIN
        )
        
        # Placement: Middle of the right side (Row C, Cols 2-5)
        # Using scale 1.0 initially to avoid double scaling in place_in_area
        self.place_in_area(formula, "C2", "C5", scale_factor=1.2)

class TeachingScene(Scene):

        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)

            for j, col in enumerate(cols):

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the layout with provided title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout(
            "The Shape of the Distribution",
            [
                "A histogram visualizes how probabilities shift with n and p.",
                "Low p-values skew the distribution toward the left.",
                "As trials increase, the shape resembles a smooth bell curve."
            ]
        )

        def binomial_pmf(n, p, k):
            if k < 0 or k > n:
                return 0
            return math.comb(n, k) * (p**k) * ((1-p)**(n-k))

        def get_chart(n, p, bar_color):
            values = [binomial_pmf(n, p, k) for k in range(n + 1)]
            # Create a bar chart. Using BarChart class from Manim Community.
            chart = BarChart(
                values=values,
                bar_names=[str(k) for k in range(n + 1)],
                y_range=[0, 0.45, 0.1],
                x_length=5.5,
                y_length=4,
                axis_config={"font_size": 18},
                bar_colors=[bar_color] * (n + 1)
            )
            return chart

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show a symmetrical histogram for n=10, p=0.5 in white (#FFFFFF).
        n_val = 10
        p1 = 0.5
        chart = get_chart(n_val, p1, WHITE)
        # Using C2-F6 to stay below Row B and avoid clipping at Col 6
        self.place_in_area(chart, "C2", "F6", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        params = VGroup(
            Text(f"n = {n_val}", font_size=24, color=WHITE),
            Text(f"p = {p1}", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(params, "B4", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))

        self.wait(2)

        chart2 = get_chart(n_val, p2, "#FF9999")

        params2 = VGroup(
            Text(f"n = {n_val}", font_size=24, color="#FF9999"),
            Text(f"p = {p2}", font_size=24, color="#FF9999")
        ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(params2, "B4", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF9999"))
        self.play(
            Transform(chart, chart2),
            Transform(params, params2),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.play(Indicate(chart))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Shift bars right for p=0.9, coloring them light blue (#9999FF).
        p3 = 0.9
        chart3 = get_chart(n_val, p3, "#9999FF")
        self.place_in_area(chart3, "C2", "F6", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        params3 = VGroup(
            Text(f"n = {n_val}", font_size=24, color="#9999FF"),
            Text(f"p = {p3}", font_size=24, color="#9999FF")
        ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(params3, "B4", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#9999FF"))
        self.play(

        )

outline.topic: Mastering the Binomial Distribution: The Math of 'Yes' or 'No'
outline.target_audience: High school or introductory college statistics students

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Bernoulli Trial
sections.content: Introduce the simplest building block of probability: a single event with only two outcomes (Success or Failure). Define 'p' as the probability of success and 'q' (1-p) as the probability of failure. This sets the stage for multiple trials.
sections.example: A hungry frog attempts to catch a fly. Either he catches it (Success) or he doesn't (Failure). This single snap is a Bernoulli trial.

sections.title: The B.I.N.S. Criteria
sections.content: Define the four conditions required for a distribution to be considered 'Binomial' using the acronym BINS: Binary (Success/Failure), Independent (one trial doesn't affect the next), Number (fixed number of trials 'n'), and Same (probability 'p' stays constant).
sections.example: A robot shoots 5 basketball free throws. 1. Success/Miss (Binary). 2. One shot doesn't affect the next (Independent). 3. Exactly 5 shots (Number). 4. The robot's programming gives it a constant 70% accuracy (Same probability).

sections.title: Visualizing Combinations: The 'How Many Ways' Logic
sections.content: Explain that in multiple trials, there are different ways to achieve the same number of successes. Use a tree diagram animation to show how paths branch out, leading to the combination formula nCr (n choose k).
sections.example: If the robot shoots twice, there is 1 way to get 2 hits (SS), but 2 ways to get 1 hit (SF or FS). Visualizing these paths explains why the center of the distribution is often taller.

sections.title: The Binomial Formula Breakdown
sections.content: Present the formula: P(X=k) = (nCk) * (p^k) * (q^(n-k)). Use color-coding to link each part of the formula to the visual elements discussed: Orange for 'Ways to win', Blue for 'Probability of winning', and Red for 'Probability of losing'.
sections.example: To find the chance of the frog catching exactly 3 flies out of 5 attempts: Combine the number of 3-fly sequences with the math of (Success probability)^3 and (Failure probability)^2.

sections.title: The Shape of the Distribution
sections.content: Show how the binomial distribution looks as a histogram. Demonstrate how changing 'n' (number of trials) and 'p' (probability) alters the shape. Emphasize that when p=0.5, the graph is perfectly symmetrical, but as 'p' nears 0 or 1, it becomes skewed.
sections.example: An animation showing a histogram shifting: If p=0.1 (hard task), the bars cluster on the left. If p=0.9 (easy task), they cluster on the right. If n increases to 50, the shape begins to look like a smooth Bell Curve.

sections.title: Real-World Application: Quality Control
sections.content: Conclude by applying the concept to a practical scenario. This reinforces why the binomial distribution is essential for predicting outcomes in manufacturing, science, and business.
sections.example: A factory drone inspects a batch of 10 sensors. If 5% of sensors are usually defective, what is the probability that exactly 0 are broken in this batch? Using the formula, we find there's a 59.9% chance the whole batch is perfect.

storyboard.title: The B.I.N.S. Criteria
lecture_lines: Binomial distributions must meet four specific criteria, called BINS.
"B" stands for Binary: outcomes are either success or failure.
"I" means Independent: one trial doesn't affect the next.
"N" is for Number: there's a fixed amount of trials.
"S" stands for Same: the probability p remains constant.

storyboard.title: Visualizing Combinations: The 'How Many Ways' Logic
lecture_lines: Multiple trials create many different paths to the same result.
A tree diagram helps visualize these branching possibilities.
For two shots, there are two ways to hit once.
We use the combination formula to count these unique paths.

storyboard.title: The Binomial Formula Breakdown

First, count the number of ways to get k successes.
Next, multiply by the probability of those successes occurring.
Then, multiply by the probability of the remaining failures.
Together, these three parts form the complete binomial equation.
